rationale: The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the measured experiment example batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, which added timeout-minutes to a checks job and preserved all successful conclusions while reducing elapsed time. The repository's CI history shows representative successful-duration history (successful runs completing in roughly 6-8 minutes), satisfying the pattern precondition, and adding a timeout only bounds runaway consumption without removing any build/test step or changing required checks. I applied a 10-minute timeout to the checks job, which is above the checks portion of observed runs so valid slow runs are not cut off (respecting the contraindication that valid slow runs must not exceed the limit), while capping runaway jobs. No permissions, secrets, deployment, or new network access is introduced.
